assay_comments: There are two molecules in the crystallographic asymmetric unit. PDB chains for each complex are: Complex I: MHC α-chain: A, β2-m chain: B, epitope chain: C, TCR α-chain: D, TCR β-chain: E. Complex II: MHC α-chain: F, β2-m chain: G, epitope chain: H, TCR α-chain: K, TCR β-chain: L. One important difference between the two molecules is that MHC residue Q155, located at the interface between the MHC and the CDR2α, adopts two different conformations. In the first molecule (AV-wt1, complex I), it contacts S51 of CDR2α, while in the other molecule (AV-wt2, complex II), it points toward T94 of TCRα. Also, one molecule has an interface area that was similar to that seen in the 1G4-HLA-A2/NY-ESO-1 structure [PDB: 2BNR], while the other is similar to that of the C49c50 mutant structure [PDB: 2F53]. This assay refers to the complex I (AV-wt1).

These chains were identified from high affinity TCR clones in ELISA experiments. This C49c50 mutant yielded a soluble TCR with an affinity of 1 nM. There was no electron density for the C-terminal 14 residues of TCRβ, which were removed from the final model. immunization_comments: The IG4 CTL clone was established from mixed lymphocyte cultures of PBMC and the autologous tumor cell line NW-MEL-38 from a patient with malignant melanoma. The AV-wt  TCR was obtained from the rearranged Vα and Vß open reading frames of the native 1G4 TCR (TRAV21, TRBV6–5), which were cloned into a phagemid vector, pEX922, adjacent to their respective vector-encoded Cα and Cß domains that had been modified to allow disulfide-assisted heterodimerization of the two chains. The CDR2α and CDR2ß loops of the human parental IG4 TCR were randomly mutated and the phage-displayed TCRs were selected for binding to the epitope/HLA-A*0201 complex. Combining the α chain c49wt with wtc50 ß chain generated the high affinity mutant c49c50 TCR. Soluble TCR molecules were expressed and purified.

assay_comments: There are four molecules in the crystallographic asymmetric unit. PDB chains for each complex are: Complex I: MHC α-chain: A, β2-m chain: B, epitope chain: C, TCR α-chain: D, TCR β-chain: E. Complex II: MHC α-chain: F, β2-m chain: G, epitope chain: H, TCR α-chain: I, TCR β-chain: J. Complex III: MHC α-chain: K, β2-m chain: L, epitope chain: M, TCR α-chain: N, TCR β-chain: P. Complex IV: MHC α-chain: Q, β2-m chain: R, epitope chain: S, TCR α-chain: T, TCR β-chain: U. All TCR-MHC/epitope complexes had well ordered electron density, and the electron density at the TCR-MHC/epitope interface was unambiguous. The individual TCR and MHC/epitope components were almost identical in all complexes. But, there was a TCR-MHC/epitope dimer present in the crystal lattice, made by complexes A (complex I) and B (complex IV). These complexes have distinct conformations, with the TCR adopting two different docking strategies on the MHC/epitope complex that differed by 12 degrees. This rotation axis was parallel to the peptide binding groove, causing atomic shifts in excess of 7 Å, resulting in leaning of the TCR more toward the MHC α2-helix. This assay refers to Complex A (complex I).
immunization_comments: Generation of the T Cell clone SB27 was previously described in the reference cited: Tynan et al. (2005) J Biol Chem 280: 23900-23909 [PMID: 15849183]. The SB27 TCR was expressed and purified.

assay_comments: There are two molecules in the crystallographic asymmetric unit. PDB chains for each complex are: Complex I: MHC α-chain: A, β2-m chain: B, epitope chain: C, TCR α-chain: D, TCR β-chain: E. Complex II: MHC α-chain: F, β2-m chain: G, epitope chain: H, TCR α-chain: K, TCR β-chain: L. One important difference between the two molecules is that MHC residue Q155, located at the interface between the MHC and the CDR2α, adopts two different conformations. In the first molecule (AV-wt1, complex I), it contacts S51 of CDR2α, while in the other molecule (AV-wt2, complex II), it points toward T94 of TCRα. Also, one molecule has an interface area that was similar to that seen in the 1G4-HLA-A2/NY-ESO-1 structure [PDB: 2BNR], while the other is similar to that of the C49c50 mutant structure [PDB: 2F53]. This assay refers to the complex II (AV-wt2).
immunization_comments: The IG4 CTL clone was established from mixed lymphocyte cultures of PBMC and the autologous tumor cell line NW-MEL-38 from a patient with malignant melanoma. Soluble TCR molecules were expressed and purified.

assay_comments: Reactivity against peptide-pulsed, A*0201+ T2 cells was tested for transduced CD8+ T cells expressing the WT TCR or single- or double-residue TCR mutants, showing that CD8+ T cells expressing the WT TCR or with mutations at αCDR3 positions 95 and 96 had similar levels of reactivity. Mutations at βCDR2 positions 51, 52 and 54 enhanced reactivity, but a construct encoding three substitutions at positions 51, 52, and 54 ( 51:AI-T) led to the nonspecific recognition of HLA-A*02+ T2 cells when pulsed with a noncognate control peptide. βCDR3 substitution variants at positions 96, 97 and 98 most resulted in a diminished T cell response.
immunization_comments: The A2-restricted epitope-specific 1G4 CTL was derived from a melanoma patient as described in the cited reference: Jager et al. (1988) J Exp Med 187: 265-270 [PMID: 9432985]. CTL were established by stimulation of the patient's PBLs with autologous NY-ESO-1-positive tumor-derived cell lines. The 1G4 TCR was cloned, and used to transfect CD8+ or CD4+ T cell populations from PBMCs previously activated with OKT-3 anti-CD3 Ab for 5 to 21 days. Single and double amino acid substitutions were included in the CDRs by PCR.

assay_comments: Tumor infiltrating lymphocyte(TIL)-derived T cell clones were stained with the epitope-MHC tetramer with different relative affinities. Representative clones were chosen from each (low, medium or high) category and TCR α and β genes were isolated. The use of a mutant MHC that binds independent of CD8 showed that the high affinity TCRs could bind it. Five of seven clones showed Vα region 12-2 restriction, and a sixth clone consisted of the closely related Vα12-3, confirming previous reports of a strong TCR α variable region restriction in recognition of MART-1 Ag. TCR transfection into syngeneic CD8+ PBMCs or TILs showed that they retain the ability to react to the epitope-MHC tetramer.
immunization_comments: T cell clones were derived from melanoma tumors from three patients, after incubation in vitro with IL-2 and epitope-tetramer sorting of specific cells, by limiting dilution.

immunization_comments: Isolation of the parent 1G4 TCR was described in cited reference [PMID: 9432985].  The IG4 CTL clone was established from mixed lymphocyte cultures of PBMC and the autologous tumor cell line NW-MEL-38 from a patient with malignant melanoma. The 1G4 TCR genes were cloned into a phagemid vector followed by random mutation of the CDR2α and CDR2ß loops and selection of the phage-displayed TCRs for binding to the epitope/HLA-A*0201 complex to obtain high affinity mutant TCRs 1G4-c50 and 1G4-c53c50. assay_comments: Jurkat cells expressing the TCRs were activated by HLA-A*11:01+ K562 pulsed with the epitope, assessed by CD69 expression. Analysis of  a single- substitution peptide scanning library of the epitope showed that the parental KT5 TCR only recognized substitutions at a few N-terminal positions. The CDR3β variant TCRs (KT5-B1, KT5-B2, Kt5-B3 and KT5-B4) displayed increased tolerance against mutations at the N-terminal positions and varying degrees of reduced speciﬁcity at G8 and V9.
immunization_comments: Generation of the T cell clone was previously described in the cited reference: [PMID: 39819441]. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from healthy donors. CD8+ T cells were co-cultured with DCs pulsed with KRAS(G12D) peptide. KRAS(G12D) specific T cells were identified by tetramer staining and the TCRs were cloned. KT5 TCR variants with improved functional avidity and speciﬁcity were selected from two libraries, one targeting the CDR3α region and the other the CDR3β region by screening them using an iterative selection strategy that included positive selection with KRAS(G12D)-pulsed antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and negative selection with KRAS WT-pulsed APCs.
